verses.text: When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went into the LORD's temple.
He sent Eliakim, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and the leading priests, all wearing sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
They told him, "This is what Hezekiah says: 'Today is a day of trouble, punishment, and shame. We are like a woman who is ready to give birth, but has no strength to deliver the baby.

Perhaps the LORD your God will hear all the words of the field commander, whom his master the king of Assyria sent to insult the living God. Perhaps the LORD your God will punish him for the words he has heard. So pray for the few of us who are still left.'"
When King Hezekiah's officials came to Isaiah,
Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master, 'This is what the LORD says: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, the insults the king of Assyria's servants have spoken against me.
Listen! I will put a spirit in him so that when he hears a certain report, he will go back to his own country. And there in his own country I will have him killed with the sword.'"
The field commander heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish. So he went back and found the king fighting against Libnah.
Then the king of Assyria heard that Tirhakah, the king of Ethiopia, was marching out to fight against him. So he again sent messengers to Hezekiah with this message:
"Tell Hezekiah king of Judah: 'Do not let the God you trust fool you when he says, "Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria."
Surely you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the other countries. They destroyed them completely. Do you think you will be rescued?
Did the gods of the nations my ancestors destroyed rescue them? Did the gods rescue Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden who lived in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath? Where is the king of Arpad? Where are the kings of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?'"
Hezekiah took the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the LORD's temple and spread it out before the LORD.
Hezekiah prayed to the LORD: "LORD, God of Israel, you sit on your throne above the cherubim. You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made heaven and earth.
Turn your ear, LORD, and listen. Open your eyes, LORD, and see. Listen to the words Sennacherib has sent to insult the living God.
It is true, LORD, that the kings of Assyria have destroyed these nations and their lands.
They have thrown their gods into the fire, because they were not gods at all. They were only wood and stone made by human hands. That is why the Assyrians could destroy them.
So now, LORD our God, please save us from his power, so that all the kingdoms of the earth will know that you alone, LORD, are God."
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent this message to Hezekiah: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I have heard your prayer about Sennacherib king of Assyria.
This is the word the LORD has spoken against him: The young woman, the city of Zion, hates you and laughs at you. The city of Jerusalem shakes her head at you as you run away.
Who have you insulted and mocked? Who have you shouted against and looked down on so proudly? It was the Holy One of Israel!

Through your messengers you have insulted the Lord. You have said, "With my many chariots I have climbed the highest mountains, the farthest heights of Lebanon. I have cut down its tallest cedars and its best pine trees. I have reached its farthest places and its thickest forests.
I have dug wells in foreign lands and drunk their water. With the soles of my feet I have dried up all the streams of Egypt."
Have you not heard? Long ago I planned it. In days of old I designed it, and now I have made it happen. I let you turn walled cities into piles of rubble.
That is why their people had no strength. They were frightened and ashamed. They were like grass in the field, like tender green plants, like grass on a roof that dries up before it can grow.
But I know when you sit down, when you go out, and when you come in. I know how you rage against me.
Because you rage against me, and because I have heard your proud words, I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your mouth. I will make you go back the way you came.'

This will be the sign for you, Hezekiah: This year you will eat what grows by itself, and next year what springs up from that. But in the third year you will plant and harvest, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
The people of Judah who have escaped and are left will again put roots down deep and bear fruit above.
A group of survivors will come out of Jerusalem, and people who escaped will come from Mount Zion. The LORD's burning love will make this happen.

So this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: 'He will not come into this city or shoot even one arrow here. He will not come near it with a shield or build a ramp of dirt against its walls.
He will go back the same way he came. He will not come into this city, says the LORD.
I will defend this city and save it, for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David.'"
That night the LORD's angel went out and killed one hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the Assyrian camp. When the people got up early the next morning, there were dead bodies everywhere.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and went home. He stayed in Nineveh.

One day, while he was worshipping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. His son Esarhaddon became king after him.
